sentences.text:
Ssmt.Beena vs Mrs.Kundatai Rajendra Sarnobat on 14 August,
2024
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Surender
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 1748 Of 2009
Judgment:

1. The appellants, who are petitioners in the lower Court were denied compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad vide judgment in O.P.No.198 of 2005, dated 17.06.2008 on the ground that the deceased was negligent and he was responsible for the accident.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- II Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The parties hereinafter will be referred to as arrayed in the Original Petition before the Tribunal.
Briefly, the case of the claimants is that three vehicles were involved in the accident.
The deceased along with P.W.1 were traveling in Indica Car.
The said vehicle was sandwiched in between Milk Tanker (TATA) bearing No.MH-13B-3150 and Volvo Truck No.GJI-UU-9430.
The 1st respondent is the owner of the Milk Tanker and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the said tanker.
The 3rd respondent is the owner of the Volvo Truck and 4th respondent is the insurer of the Volvo truck.
The 5th respondent is the owner of the Indica car bearing No. MH 24F 3049 and 6th respondent is the insurer of the said Indica Car.
3. It is the case of the claimant/P.W.1 that her husband was driving the Indica car when the accident had taken place while overtaking Milk tanker.
The driver of the Milk Tanker allowed the deceased to over take his vehicle.
While overtaking the vehicle, the Volvo truck which was coming in the opposite direction, was driven in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the Indica Car.
At the same time, Milk Tanker was also responsible for the accident.
Claim petition was filed against all the three vehicle owners and the insurers under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for total sum of Rs.22,50,000/-.
The claim was made on the ground that all the drivers of three vehicles were responsible for the accident and accordingly, compensation has to be paid by all the three vehicle insurers.
4. Learned Tribunal Judge while disposing the claim found that the compensation that is liable to be paid is Rs.12,27,650/-.

However, since the deceased, who was driving the Tata Indica car overtook the heavy vehicle, which is Tata Tanker (Milk tanker) and he failed to observe Volvo truck in the opposite direction while overtaking the Milk Tanker, it resulted in the accident.

Accordingly,
negligence cannot be attributed to either the Milk Tanker driver or the Driver of the Volvo truck, but the deceased himself who was driving the Indica Car.
Further, the learned Tribunal Judge placed reliance on the charge sheet and investigation being closed mainly on the ground that the deceased was responsible for the accident.

1 5.
Learned counsel appearing for the appellants would submit that as found by the Tribunal, the entire fault cannot be attributed to the deceased.
Inferences were drawn only on the basis of the final report filed by the police, ignoring the statement of P.W.1, who was sitting in the car when accident took place.

Since the accident was on account of the negligence of the drivers of the Milk Tanker and Volvo truck, who failed to drive cautiously causing accident, compensation as claimed should be paid by all the three vehicle insurers.

6. Learned counsel relied on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Khenyei v.
New India Assurance Company Limited and others (2015) 9 Supreme Court Cases 273), wherein the Hon'ble Three Judge Bench of the Hon'le Supreme Court was dealing with joint tortfeasors liability.

entities.text:
Khenyei v.
New India Assurance Company Limited and others (2015) 9 Supreme Court Cases 273)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court held that even if one of the Joint tortfeasors involved in the accident was impleaded, then he would be liable to pay entire compensation irrespective of the other joint tortfesors being made party or not.
7.
Learned counsel also relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kamlesh and others v. Attar Singh and others (2015) 15 Supreme Court Cases 364).

entities.text: Kamlesh and others v. Attar Singh and others (2015) 15 Supreme Court Cases 364)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In National Insurance Company Limited v. Balakrishnan and another (2013)(1)SCC (CRI) 677),wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that a comprehensive package policy would cover the liability of the insurer for payment of compensation of occupants in a car unlike the Act policy.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Balakrishnan and another (2013)(1)SCC (CRI) 677),wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In National Insurance Company Limited v. Chamundeswari and others (2021) 18 Supreme Court Cases 596), the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the FIR cannot form basis for the Tribunal to decide the manner in which the accident has taken place.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Chamundeswari and others (2021) 18 Supreme Court Cases 596)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is for the Tribunal to arrive at its own conclusions on the basis of evidence adduced during trial.
9. P.W.1, who is the wife of the deceased was traveling in the car.
It is not the case of P.W.1 that the deceased was holding valid driving licence to drive the car.
Tribunal found that the deceased was not holding valid driving licence to drive the car.
10. According to P.W.1, the accident had taken place when the deceased was overtaking Milk tanker and driver of the Milk Tanker permitted him to overtake.
However, the driver of Volvo truck coming in the opposite direction had caused the accident and Indica car was sandwiched in between both the Milk Tanker and Volvo truck.
The closure of the case by the police finding the deceased negligent of the accident cannot completely form basis to reject the claim.

On the basis of the evidence adduced before the court and by reconstructing the possible manner in which the accident has taken place, the Tribunal can always come to a conclusion contrary to the finding of police during investigation.
11. According to P.W.1, Milk Tanker driver had given signal to India car to overtake the vehicle.

However, the accident happened when the Indica car was crushed in between the right side of the tanker and right side of the Volvo Truck which came from opposite direction and crushed Indica car in between.
It clearly reflects that while giving way to the India car, Milk tanker driver did not take caution nor indicate to the opposite vehicle/Volvo Truck.

It is apparent that while the car was overtaking the Tata Tanker, the Tata Tanker driver failed to take caution after allowing the car to Ssmt.Beena vs Mrs.Kundatai Rajendra Sarnobat on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102068559/
2 overtake.
In the meanwhile, the Volvo truck coming in the opposite direction hit the Indica Car.
It cannot be said that when the Indica Car was overtaking the Tanker, the driver of the Volvo truck was not able to view both the vehicles, which were on the road.
Apparently, the manner in which the accident has taken place indicates that the driver of the car, Tanker and Volvo truck were all responsible.
12. Since all the three vehicles are responsible, insurance companies of the respective vehicles are also liable to pay at 1/3rd of compensation each.
However, it is on record that the deceased was not holding valid driving licence and accordingly, insurance company of the car cannot be made liable to pay compensation.

13. The Tribunal arrived at the annual income of the deceased at Rs.1,35,000/- on the basis of the income tax returns and the computation filed under Exs.A27 to 32 for the assessment years 2003-2004, 2002-2003, 2001-2002, 2003-2004, 2002-2003 and 2001-2002.

Loss of future prospectus, as per the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company v. Pranay Sethi (2017 ACJ 2700) is at the rate of 40% of income for the persons of the age around 33 years i.e., 40% of Rs.1,35,000/- comes to Rs.54,000/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Company v. Pranay Sethi (2017 ACJ 2700)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Then total income of the deceased per annum is Rs.1,89,000/-.
If 1/4th of the income is deducted towards his personal and living expenses as per the Judgment of Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, it comes to Rs.47,250/- per annum.

entities.text: Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Then the total annual income after deduction towards personal expenses comes to Rs.1,41,750/-.
The appropriate multiplier applied for the persons of the age of the deceased is 16 as per the judgment of Praynay Sethi's case.

If the same is applied, it comes to Rs.22,68,000/-
(Rs.1,41,750/- x 16) towards loss of dependency.
14. The respondents/claimants are entitled for consortium of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rs.40,000/- each) to respondents 1 to 5, who are wife, children and mother of the deceased respectively.

In addition to the above, the claimants also entitled for loss of estate of Rs.15,000/- and funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- i.e., Rs.30,000/-.
15.

Therefore, in all, the claimants are entitled to the compensation as follows:
1. Loss of dependency : Rs.22,68,000/-
2. Loss of consortium : Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rs.40,000/- each)
3. Loss of estate + funeral expenses : Rs. 30,000/-.
____________________ Total: : Rs.24,98,000/-
____________________ 16.

Since this court finds that all the three vehicles are equally responsible for the accident, the compensation arrived at is liable to be paid at 1/3rd each by the three insurance companies i.e.,
respondents 2, 4 and 6.

However, since the deceased was not holding valid driving licence, the Ssmt.Beena vs Mrs.Kundatai Rajendra Sarnobat on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102068559/
3 insurer of the Indica Car is not liable and 1/3rd amount shall be deducted i.e., Rs.8,32,666/-
rounded off to Rs.8,33,000/-.
If the same is deducted from total compensation, it comes to Rs.16,65,000/-.

17. In the result, appeal is allowed and the respondents 2 & 4/insurance companies are liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount of Rs.16,65,000/- i.e, Rs.8,32,500/- each to the claimants at the rate of 7.5% from the date of appeal till the date of realization.
On such deposit, all the claimants are entitled to equal share and permitted to withdraw their respective shares as and when deposited.
18. Accordingly, the Appeal is allowed in part.
